The Shade Tree Commission & Oak-Wilt Calendar

Chagrin Falls has an active Shade Tree Commission that reviews tree work involving public right-of-way and historic-district properties. Roubic coordinates the village permit and commission review process as part of the job — we know the village contacts, the application forms, and the review timelines. Private-property pruning generally does not require a permit; ROW and historic-district work does.

Oak species carry a hard scheduling rule: no oak pruning April 1 through July 31, to prevent oak-wilt vector exposure during sap-feeding beetle activity. Everything else runs on the dormant-season rotation in February and early March, when pruning wounds heal cleanest heading into spring.

Permit coordination confirmed at estimate — any fees billed at cost, no markup

What Happens If You Defer

The Cost of Waiting — Chagrin Falls Context

Three ways a routine pruning bill turns into a much larger job when it's deferred.

EAB Ash Decline

Ash left unmanaged past first symptoms move from prunable to hazardous fast. Once structural failure sets in, a $600 pruning visit becomes a full removal job over structures.

Deadwood & Wind Load

Chagrin Falls' mature ornamental canopy takes hard March–May wind hits. Uncleared deadwood and dense crowns become the branches that come down on roofs and cars.

Oak-Wilt Window Miss

Miss the dormant window and any oak work waits until after July 31 — a full season lost. Rushed off-calendar oak cuts risk oak-wilt vector exposure across the whole canopy.

Common Chagrin Falls Pruning Questions

Chagrin Falls Tree Trimming & Pruning FAQ

Six things Chagrin Falls homeowners want to know before booking.

How much does tree pruning cost in Chagrin Falls?
Pruning in Chagrin Falls typically runs $250–$1,500 per tree depending on size, species, and access. Multi-tree dormant-rotation contracts qualify for 10–15% package savings under per-tree rates. Most Chagrin Falls dormant pruning work is scheduled between February and early March. Every estimate is free and written on-site.
When is the best time to prune trees in Chagrin Falls?
For most Chagrin Falls canopy species, late winter (February through early March) is the ideal window — trees are dormant, sap flow is minimized, and pruning wounds have the cleanest healing response heading into spring growth. The exception is oak species, which we never prune between April 1 and July 31 due to oak-wilt vector exposure during sap-feeding beetle activity.
Do I need a permit to prune trees in Chagrin Falls?
Trees on public right-of-way in Chagrin Falls, and work in the historic district, require coordination with the village's Shade Tree Commission; private-property pruning generally does not. Roubic confirms permit requirements at the estimate and coordinates the application and review process on your behalf — any fees are billed at cost and disclosed upfront.
What's the difference between crown reduction and crown thinning?
Crown reduction shortens the overall canopy size by selectively cutting back to lateral branches — used to reduce wind exposure or clearance issues. Crown thinning removes select interior branches to reduce density without changing overall size — used to improve light penetration and reduce wind-loading. Both follow ANSI A300 cuts and never exceed 25% live-canopy removal in a single visit.
Does Roubic offer multi-tree pruning contracts in Chagrin Falls?
Yes. Multi-tree maintenance contracts are available across Chagrin Falls on a dormant-season rotation in late winter. Most contracts qualify for 10–15% package savings under per-tree pricing and lock in the same crew year over year for canopy continuity.
Does Roubic top trees?
No — Roubic never tops trees and never lion-tails mature canopy. Topping creates weak regrowth, decay entry points, and long-term structural problems, especially on the 50 to 100+ year-old canopy common in Chagrin Falls. Every cut follows ANSI A300 standards, and we cap live-canopy removal at 25% per visit to keep trees healthy.
